transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Verdant Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Verdant Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Verdant Security)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Marcus, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Daniel Ruiz: Doing good, thanks. Ready to dig in.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Hi all, Marcus here. Quick agenda from our side - run through how you'd integrate with Redwood (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex), discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and cover observability and rate limiting. Sound OK?
[00:23] Priya Nair: Yep that sounds perfect. We're mostly interested in practical integration patterns.
[00:27] Samir Patel: And security  encryption at rest, KMS, audit logs, SSO, that sort of thing.
[00:33] Ava Chen: Great. Quick context check - Priya, Daniel, can you describe your stack? Where are you running your retrieval/embeddings today?
[00:40] Priya Nair: Sure. We run our RAG pipelines in k8s on GCP. For embeddings we use OpenAI's embeddings for now, and we orchestrate chains through LangChain and Llama-Index, we have a vector DB (Pinecone) for most products.
[00:55] Daniel Ruiz: We're multi-tenant, tenant routing happens at our API gateway, and we do per-tenant quotas. We want to evaluate Redwood to potentially replace or supplement the OpenAI calls, and/or run Dedicated for tighter SLAs.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: OK good, that maps to a few common patterns. Integration is usually straightforward: we have official Python and JavaScript SDKs, plus REST. Folks using LangChain/Llama-Index typically wrap the Redwood SDK in the LangChain connectors or use the Llama-Index client. We also publish example notebooks and repo samples.
[01:28] Priya Nair: About the LangChain connector  is there an official adapter? We've seen community adapters but wanted to know Redwood provided ones.
[01:36] Marcus Lee: Yes, we maintain a LangChain connector and a Llama-Index integration. I'll share the links. Note that some community examples call our REST endpoint through a gateway; both approaches work. The official connector supports streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.
[01:51] Daniel Ruiz: How's streaming handled in the SDK? We have a bunch of low-latency customer-facing features that need token-level streaming.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: Streaming is supported in both SDKs; in Python we provide an async iterator that yields tokens or events. There's also an SSE/HTTP stream option. We can attach cancellation hooks if a user drops the connection. Some transcription errors: sometimes the SSE events get named slightly differently depending on client libs but nothing major.
[02:17] Priya Nair: Good. Next, rate limits  we need hard quotas per tenant and a burst model. Right now we throttle at the gateway layer. Would we route through Redwood directly, or send traffic through our proxy?
[02:30] Ava Chen: Two options: 1) call Redwood API directly from your backend with per-tenant API keys you mint, or 2) route through your gateway/proxy to apply policy before hitting Redwood. Many customers prefer option 2 for consistent billing and routing. We also support a gateway mode where you can run a lightweight proxy in your VPC that does authentication and enforces quotas locally before forwarding.
[02:51] Daniel Ruiz: That gateway/proxy option  is it open source or a container we run?
[02:55] Marcus Lee: It's a small containerized proxy we provide as part of Private deployments and as an optional artifact for Dedicated customers. You run it in your infra; it supports token minting, per-tenant routing, rate-limit enforcement, and basic telemetry forwarding. Sometimes we call it the redwood-gw internally, docs sometimes say 'redwood-proxy'  transcription note: docs sometimes show BPC instead of VPC  ignore that.
[03:18] Samir Patel: From a security POV we need KMS integration and the ability to keep keys in our account. How does that work?
[03:25] Marcus Lee: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM via Cloud KMS or external HSMs; Dedicated has a KMS integration where keys can be customer-managed in some configurations. For hosted API we manage keys but we do offer encrypted-at-rest with our KMS and we can discuss bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on a case-by-case enterprise plan.
[03:45] Priya Nair: And audit logs? We need request-level logs and token accounting per request for billing and cost attribution.
[03:53] Ava Chen: We provide per-request metadata and trace IDs, and our Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns. For Dedicated and Private we ship raw audit logs (JSON) to your S3 or GCS bucket and provide integrations with SIEMs. Hosted can export logs to your cloud via loghooks on enterprise plans.
[04:12] Daniel Ruiz: Nice. For rate limiting, can we have different quotas per model and per route? Eg embeddings have different cost model than generation.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: Yes  quotas are per-route and per-model. You can set token-based quotas, request-count quotas, and burst windows. There's also per-customer policy rules so you can say tenant A gets X tokens/day for embeddings, Y for gen, etc.
[04:36] Priya Nair: How about observability hooks  we'd like tracing (X-Request-ID), latency breakdown, and per-call token counts in traces so we can label traces with cost info.
[04:46] Marcus Lee: We emit trace IDs and support attaching your trace context. Our Console shows per-route latency and token histograms. We can also send trace spans to your tracer (Jaeger/Zipkin/OTel) in Dedicated/Private; hosted supports OTLP ingest on enterprise.
[05:02] Samir Patel: Compliance  SOC2, ISO certifications?
[05:06] Ava Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO attestation in process  I'll share the latest certs. Also we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, and org-level audit logs.
[05:17] Daniel Ruiz: One of our concerns is cost predictability. If we move away from OpenAI embeddings to Redwood embeddings, do you offer batching/caching that reduces token costs?
[05:28] Marcus Lee: Absolutely. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on batching and quantization for model selection. On runtime we have automatic prefix/KV caching that reduces repeated context costs, and continuous batching for throughput. For embeddings we support on-demand batching and reuse of cached vectors; cost reduction depends on access patterns but customers report 20-40% lower token spend in typical RAG flows after optimization.
[05:52] Priya Nair: You mentioned KV caching  is that the same as the KV cache behind transformers to avoid re-sending previous tokens?
[05:59] Marcus Lee: Yes, it's the attention/KV cache mechanism that keeps state between tokens for a session. We also do prefix caching for repeated prompts. In docs sometimes transcription shows 'KV cash'  that is the same.
[06:10] Daniel Ruiz: For our benchmarking, we need to test both throughput and latency at 95th/99th percentiles. Can you run a pilot where you provision Dedicated capacity for our tests?
[06:21] Marcus Lee: We can do a short pilot. Typical approach: we spin up a small Dedicated pool or a hosted benchmark campaign with pinned model versions, run your prompt set, and produce p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. We'll need sample prompts and target SLAs.
[06:36] Ava Chen: For timing, Marcus and I can send a pilot plan. Priya, can you share the prompt set and expected concurrency?
[06:44] Priya Nair: We'll share that. Expected concurrency is about 120 concurrent sessions, spikes to 500 for short bursts. Average response length ~120 tokens.
[06:54] Marcus Lee: That's helpful. For that workload we'd likely recommend Dedicated with autoscale and burst capacity; hosted can handle it but Dedicated gives more predictable latency.
[07:05] Daniel Ruiz: What about multi-region? Some of our users are EU-only; we need data residency.
[07:12] Ava Chen: We have hosted regions in NA and EU, and Dedicated/Private can be deployed in specific regions or on-prem. For strict data residency we recommend Private (VPC) so data and keys stay in your environment.
[07:23] Samir Patel: Could you summarize the differences at a high level? Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[07:28] Marcus Lee: Sure. Hosted: fastest time-to-value, managed keys, shared multi-tenant infra, usage-based pricing. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for a customer, predictable throughput, more isolation, optional customer-managed keys in some setups, SLA-backed latency/uptime. Private: customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem), full data residency and KMS/HSM integration, enterprise licensing.
[07:48] Priya Nair: For SDKs, do you support token-level cost headers or is that only in Console?
[07:55] Marcus Lee: We return per-response metadata including token counts and cost estimate in response headers and the SDK surfaces these programmatically. Console aggregates them. Hosted returns them too.
[08:05] Daniel Ruiz: Integration with LangChain  do you have an example of using Redwood as an LLM wrapper and using custom retriever from Llama-Index?
[08:12] Marcus Lee: Yes, code sample  basically you swap the llm client to Redwood client and adapt the streaming iterator. For Llama-Index you'd use our Llama-Index connector; we published a sample repo that shows embeddings -> store -> retriever -> index with Redwood as the embedding/llm provider. I'll link it.
[08:29] Ava Chen: Quick note on billing: we bill tokens and model units; embeddings are billed differently. If you route through your proxy you can attribute costs to tenants by passing tenant metadata on each request.
[08:41] Priya Nair: Good. Any limitations on model sizes or quantization when using Dedicated? We run some larger dense models.
[08:49] Marcus Lee: Dedicated supports a variety of model sizes; kernel selection and quantization options vary by model. For some very large models we recommend specific GPU types; we'll profile during pilot.
[09:01] Daniel Ruiz: Do you support custom model uploads or only model catalog?
[09:06] Marcus Lee: On Private you can bring your own model artifacts; Dedicated sometimes supports custom models if we coordinate. Hosted is limited to our catalog for now.
[09:15] Samir Patel: For the audit process, Samir here  what's the SLAs for log delivery and retention options? And is there an option for immutable logs?
[09:25] Ava Chen: We can deliver logs to your bucket with configurable retention. For Dedicated/Private you can set retention and we support write-once storage on your side; Redwood's audit logs are tamper-evident and we provide signed attestations on enterprise plans.
[09:40] Priya Nair: A question on quotas  can we set different quotas for embeddings rate vs generation rate and also throttle based on token consumption not just RPS?
[09:50] Marcus Lee: Yes, quotas support token-based windows and request-based windows; you can create policies that combine both.
[09:58] Daniel Ruiz: Any gotchas with LangChain agents or tool calling? We do a lot of tool calling to internal systems.
[10:05] Marcus Lee: Tool calling is supported; we integrate with function calling paradigms. The main gotcha is you need to manage tool execution latency and idempotency yourself; Redwood returns structured tool responses and supports safe retries. We'll share a pattern doc.
[10:20] Ava Chen: We should probably cover billing and procurement  Daniel, what's your procurement timeline?
[10:25] Daniel Ruiz: We're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2, procurement in early Q3. Need to run a POC in April.
[10:32] Ava Chen: Great  we'll aim to have pricing and pilot plan to you by Tuesday.
[10:36] Marcus Lee: For the pilot we'll include a benchmark plan, and options for a small Dedicated pool for stress testing.
[10:42] Priya Nair: One more thing  observability hooks: can the SDK emit spans directly to our OTLP collector?
[10:48] Marcus Lee: SDKs can emit telemetry and we support passing trace context. For direct OTLP export we recommend Dedicated/Private; hosted supports pushing traces via OTLP ingest on enterprise.
[10:58] Daniel Ruiz: Any limits on number of API keys or per-tenant keys we can mint?
[11:03] Marcus Lee: No hard limit; you can mint per-tenant keys programmatically. Keys are manageable via Console and API.
[11:10] Samir Patel: Do you maintain SOC2 docs and encryption architecture diagrams? We'd like those for our security review.
[11:15] Ava Chen: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram showing KMS integrations. Samir, we'll include contact for our security team.
[11:24] Priya Nair: Okay this is helpful. Recap next steps?
[11:28] Ava Chen: Recap: 1) We'll send hosted vs dedicated pricing and the SOC2/KMS matrix (Ava) 2) Marcus will put together a pilot/benchmark plan and sample prompt set integration notes 3) Priya will share prompt set, workload, and preferred SDK language 4) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with infra (we proposed 2026-04-01).
[11:48] Daniel Ruiz: That matches. Thanks, everyone.
[11:51] Marcus Lee: Thanks all  we'll follow up with links to LangChain/Llama-Index sample repos and the redwood-proxy container.
[11:59] Ava Chen: Alright, I'll send notes and action items. Appreciate your time.
[12:03] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[12:05] Samir Patel: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-transcribed terms (BPC/VPC, KV cash). Speaker tags sometimes simplified.

End of meeting.
